<text>
Summary of proposals (2015 manifesto)

Economy and public finances
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; lift the 40% threshold to £55,000; introduce a 30% intermediate band; abolish inheritance tax; expand transferable allowances for couples.
- Cut small business rates by 20% for properties with rateable value under £50,000.
- Reduce the deficit through: leaving the EU to save net contributions; lowering overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI; scrapping HS2; replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system; streamlining government departments and quangos.
- Tougher action on multinational tax avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.

Immigration and borders
- End freedom of movement by leaving the EU; introduce an Australian-style points system; five-year moratorium on unskilled migration; limit skilled work visas to 50,000 annually.
- Increase Border Agency staff by 2,500; count entrants and exits; no amnesty for illegal immigration.
- Five-year qualifying period for most benefits and non-urgent NHS access; require health insurance for temporary migrants and students.
- Faster asylum processing; revoke citizenship obtained by fraud; deport foreign offenders.

NHS and social care
- Invest an extra £12bn over five years: 8,000 more GPs; 20,000 nurses; 3,000 midwives; GP-led triage in A&E; £1.5bn for mental health and dementia; free hospital parking.
- Create locally elected county health boards; introduce a “Licence to Manage” for NHS managers; end new PFI; exclude the NHS from TTIP; review EU directives affecting training/clinical trials.
- Increase social care funding by £1.2bn per year; integrate health and social care under the NHS; raise Carer’s Allowance; introduce a Dignity Code; improve home-care employment standards.

Welfare, pensions and families
- Scrap the “bedroom tax”; keep Housing Benefit for under-25s; crack down on fraud; replace ATOS-style assessments with GP/specialist-led process.
- Flexible state pension window; boost pensions guidance; criminalise pension cold-calling; restore war widows’ pensions for life.
- Maintain 15 free childcare hours; tax-free childcare; deregulate to expand childminding; require wrap-around school care 8am–6pm; shared parenting presumption; overhaul child protection.

Education
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; target class sizes of 25.
- Expand grammar, technical and vocational routes; later transfer exams; first-aid in PSHE.
- STEMM tuition fee waivers for UK students who work in-discipline in the UK for five years; reform Ofsted; limit EU student loan exposure post-EU exit.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield: national register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief on first sale; bring empty homes back into use; protect green belt; local referenda on major developments.
- Restrict access to social housing and Help to Buy to long-term taxpayers/citizens; reinvest Right to Buy receipts; homelessness register; allow inheritable mortgages.

Transport
- Cancel HS2; consider South East capacity after Airports Commission; reopen Manston Airport.
- Use speed cameras only for safety; remove road tolls where possible; oppose road-pricing tech; scrap DCPC; raise levy on foreign HGVs; VED exemption for 25+ year-old vehicles.

Energy
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; end new wind/solar subsidies (honour existing); support nuclear, gas, shale (with safeguards) and coal with CCS; abolish green levies and EU ETS participation; create a shale sovereign wealth fund.

Jobs and small business
- Prioritise domestic workers; enforce minimum wage; code for zero-hours (no exclusivity, notice/pay guarantees, path to secure contracts).
- Penalise large firms for systematic late payment; pilot state-backed trade credit insurance; 30 minutes free town-centre parking; simplify public procurement; reduce regulatory burdens.

Farming, food, and animal welfare
- UK Single Farm Payment (~£80/acre) capped; premiums for organic/rare breeds; support dairy co-ops; simplify sheep ID; clearer food labelling.
- Tougher sentences for cruelty; CCTV in abattoirs; ban live exports for slaughter; support small abattoirs.

Fishing
- Leave the CFP; establish 12-mile zone and 200-mile EEZ; protect under-10m fleet; end destructive methods; manage angling proportionately.

Heritage, pubs, and tourism
- Create a Minister for Heritage and Tourism; remove VAT on listed-building repairs; planning presumption for conservation; seaside regeneration; support pubs (micro-brewery tax breaks, optional ventilated smoking rooms), oppose minimum unit pricing.

Crime, justice, and policing
- Add 3,500 frontline police/prison staff; review constabulary structures; confirm UK Bill of Rights; withdraw from EU justice measures; decriminalise TV licence non-payment; reduce FOBT stakes; expand deportation of foreign offenders; focus prison education.

Political and local reform
- National referenda via citizen initiatives; robust recall; optional open primaries; committee veto powers on appointments/spending; proportional voting; tighten postal voting.
- Local binding referenda on major planning; weekly bins where desired; tackle antisocial behaviour; curb executive pay and waste.

Trade, defence, foreign aid, and EU exit
- Leave the EU via referendum; negotiate UK–EU free-trade access; regain WTO seat; pursue global FTAs and cooperation on shared issues.
- Spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; retain nuclear deterrent; strengthen carriers; create Director of National Intelligence; oppose an EU army; waive income tax for deployed personnel.
- Reduce overseas aid to ~0.2% of GNI; focus on emergency relief, health, water/sanitation; close DFID and merge functions into the Foreign Office; prioritise trade-led development.
</text>
